entries.originalText: The testimony of a good conscience is the glory of a good man.
entries.modernizedText: The testimony of a good conscience is the glory of a good person.

entries.originalText: Have a good conscience and thou shalt ever have joy.
entries.modernizedText: Have a good conscience, and you will always have joy.

entries.originalText: A good conscience is able to bear exceeding much, and is exceeding joyful in the midst of adversities; an evil conscience is ever fearful and unquiet.
entries.modernizedText: A good conscience can bear exceedingly much and is exceedingly joyful in the midst of adversities; an evil conscience is always fearful and restless.

entries.originalText: Thou shalt rest sweetly if thy heart condemn thee not.
entries.modernizedText: You will rest sweetly if your heart does not condemn you.

entries.originalText: Never rejoice unless when thou hast done well.
entries.modernizedText: Never rejoice except when you have done well.

entries.originalText: The wicked have never true joy, nor feel internal peace, for there is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked.(1) And if they say “we are in peace, there shall no harm happen unto us, and who shall dare to do us hurt?” believe them not, for suddenly shall the wrath of God rise up against them, and their deeds shall be brought to nought, and their thoughts shall perish.
entries.modernizedText: The wicked never have true joy or feel inward peace, for there is no peace, says my God, to the wicked.(1) And if they say, “we are in peace, no harm will happen to us, and who will dare to hurt us?” do not believe them, for suddenly the wrath of God will rise up against them, their deeds will be brought to nothing, and their thoughts will perish.

entries.originalText: To glory in tribulation is not grievous to him who loveth; for such glorying is glorying in the Cross of Christ.
entries.modernizedText: To glory in tribulation is not grievous to the person who loves, for such glorying is glorying in the Cross of Christ.

entries.originalText: Brief is the glory which is given and received of men.
entries.modernizedText: Brief is the glory that is given and received by people.

entries.originalText: Sadness always goeth hand in hand with the glory of the world.
entries.modernizedText: Sadness always goes hand in hand with the glory of the world.

entries.originalText: The glory of the good is in their conscience, and not in the report of men.
entries.modernizedText: The glory of the good is in their conscience, and not in what people say of them.

entries.originalText: The joy of the upright is from God and in God, and their joy is in the truth.
entries.modernizedText: The joy of the upright is from God and in God, and their joy is in the truth.

entries.originalText: He who desireth true and eternal glory careth not for that which is temporal; and he who seeketh temporal glory, or who despiseth it from his heart, is proved to bear little love for that which is heavenly.
entries.modernizedText: The person who desires true and eternal glory does not care for temporal glory; and the person who seeks temporal glory, or who despises it from his heart, is shown to bear little love for heavenly glory.

entries.originalText: He who careth for neither praises nor reproaches hath great tranquillity of heart.
entries.modernizedText: The person who cares for neither praise nor reproach has great tranquility of heart.

entries.originalText: He will easily be contented and filled with peace, whose conscience is pure.
entries.modernizedText: The person whose conscience is pure will easily be content and filled with peace.

entries.originalText: Thou art none the holier if thou art praised, nor the viler if thou art reproached.
entries.modernizedText: You are no holier if you are praised, nor viler if you are reproached.

entries.originalText: Thou art what thou art; and thou canst not be better than God pronounceth thee to be.
entries.modernizedText: You are what you are, and you cannot be better than God declares you to be.

entries.originalText: If thou considerest well what thou art inwardly, thou wilt not care what men will say to thee.
entries.modernizedText: If you consider well what you are inwardly, you will not care what people say to you.

entries.originalText: Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart:(2) man looketh on the deed, but God considereth the intent.
entries.modernizedText: Man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart:(2) a person looks at the deed, but God considers the intent.

entries.originalText: It is the token of a humble spirit always to do well, and to set little by oneself.
entries.modernizedText: It is the mark of a humble spirit always to do well and to think little of oneself.

entries.originalText: Not to look for consolation from any created thing is a sign of great purity and inward faithfulness.
entries.modernizedText: Not to look for consolation from any created thing is a sign of great purity and inward faithfulness.

entries.originalText: He that seeketh no outward witness on his own behalf, showeth plainly that he hath committed himself wholly to God.
entries.modernizedText: The person who seeks no outward witness on his own behalf shows plainly that he has committed himself wholly to God.

entries.originalText: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, as St. Paul saith, but whom the Lord commendeth.(3) To walk inwardly with God, and not to be held by any outer affections, is the state of a spiritual man.
entries.modernizedText: For not the person who commends himself is approved, as St. Paul says, but the one whom the Lord commends.(3) To walk inwardly with God and not be held by any outward affections is the state of a spiritual person.
